notes: This detection method scores IoU 0.609, precision 0.807 and recall 0.713 on Sen1Floods11 HandLabeled test split (88 chips) at 200 m, threshold chosen on the train split. About 19% of detected pixels are expected to be false positives, and about 29% of true flooding is expected to be missed. On held-out Indian chips (28 chips, Assam, August 2016) it scores IoU 0.725 (95% range 0.564 to 0.829).

Population is a model estimate of people living in the flooded area (GHSL 2020 and WorldPop 2018), not of people displaced or harmed, and is more likely too low than too high because about 29% of flood water is expected to be missed.
2 of 14 districts were less than 90% observed (Kasaragod, Kannur), so their flooded area covers only the part the satellite saw and may understate the flooding there.

map.reason: Change appears in distinct patches, so outlines carry the meaning.

known_confusions: Radar shadow behind terrain and tall buildings is dark and can read as water.

Smooth dry surfaces such as tarmac, sand flats and bare hardpan can read as water. Measured: precision falls to 0.22 in arid Somalia and 0.32 in Pakistan, against 0.88 in Assam - treat flood maps over dry ground (Rajasthan, Kutch) with matching caution.

Flooded vegetation may NOT be detected: the canopy bounces the pulse off the trunks and back to the sensor, so water beneath trees or tall crops reads as bright rather than dark. Measured at 7.7% of all undetected water.
Wind roughens open water and raises backscatter, which can cause flooding to be underestimated during a storm.

Recall is 0.574 at 10 m and 0.713 at the 200 m analysis scale: about 29% to 43% of labelled water is still missed. Most of it is brighter than any defensible water threshold - mixed pixels, turbid or shallow water - and is a limit of single-date thresholding rather than of this particular threshold.
Boundary vintage is 2015; districts created after that date are not resolvable.

report.text: The flood map shows 663.1 km² of water [E1], representing 1.91 percent of the observable area [E2]; permanent water bodies cover 273.5 km² [E3]. A total of 92 zones were identified, with the largest zone measuring 84.52 km² [E5] and 51.8 percent of the flooded area belonging to zones larger than 0.5 km² [E6] [E4]. Modelled resident counts in the flooded extent are 17,800 people (GHSL 2020) [E7] and 109,100 people (WorldPop 2018) [E8]; baseline water was 10.9 km² [E9] and net new water is 652.2 km² [E10]. This detection method scores IoU 0.609, precision 0.807 and recall 0.713 on the Sen1Floods11 test split, with about 19 % false positives and 29 % missed flood water; population figures are model estimates and likely low because of the missed water. Two of the 14 districts (Kasaragod, Kannur) were observed at less than 90 % coverage, so their reported flooded areas may understate the true extent.
